# System 0.5

> System 0.5: Learning to Restore Nominal VLA Execution Under Unknown Low-Level Changes. Sangho Yun, Minsoo Kim and Hwanjo Yu (corresponding author), POSTECH. Project page: https://devsangho.github.io/System0.5-public/

System 0.5 is a learned layer between a frozen vision-language-action (VLA) policy and System 0 (the controller and the robot body). It corrects each command toward the nominal execution of its action chunk: the motion that the nominal System 0, the one under which the policy's demonstrations were recorded, would produce for the same chunk from the state where the chunk starts. It identifies the current System 0 from its own history of commands and measured motion and is trained on the tracking error through a learned forward model, without any task reward. Status: RSS 2027, under review; code will be released upon publication.

## Key results
- RoboStress joint faults (pi0.5, LIBERO): 72.7% success vs 56.6% best reported (SC-VLA); our pi0.5 base 51.8%.
- J-PARC joint-fault benchmark: 68.1% vs 61.7% best reported (J-PARC); our base 56.6%.
- Eight System 0 changes outside the training distribution (LIBERO-Spatial, 8 x 40 episodes): 84.7%, above pass-through (76.9%), rule-based gain (72.5%), rule-based + 4 modules (79.4%), APEX (76.3%) and residual SAC (42.8%).
- Other policies: the layer trained on pi0.5 chunks, placed unchanged below OpenVLA-OFT and GR00T N1.7, raises their success under the eight changes from 59.7 to 75.6% and from 59.4 to 80.0%; under the nominal System 0, 91.1 to 93.1% and 92.2 to 92.2% (360 episodes each).
- Reference of the layer: trained toward the command, the same layer reaches 25.6% under the eight changes (pass-through 76.9%); toward the one-tick nominal response, 66.9%.
- Tracking error and success: over the eight changes at three strengths (24 conditions), success rises more where System 0.5 lowers the tracking error more (Spearman rho = -0.51, one-sided permutation p = 0.007); over 11 methods (3,640 episodes), success falls as the error rises (rho = -0.93).
- Real UR5e (pi0.5 fine-tuned on 29 demonstrations, pick-and-place, 30 placements per method): tracking error 9.0 mm (pass-through), 1.8 mm (online gain calibrator), 1.2 mm (System 0.5), lower at every placement; median task time 114, 62 and 54 s; completed 16, 16 and 21 of 30.

## Questions and answers
### What is System 0.5?
System 0.5 is a learned layer between a frozen vision-language-action (VLA) policy and System 0, the controller and the robot body. Once per 50 ms tick it corrects the arm part of each command so that every action chunk moves the arm as it would under the System 0 that recorded the policy's demonstrations.

### What is the nominal execution of a chunk?
The nominal execution is the trajectory that the nominal System 0, the one under which the demonstrations were recorded, would produce from the state where the chunk actually starts. It restarts from the actual state at every chunk, so the error one chunk leaves is not carried into the next.

### Why not make the arm follow the command?
Under LIBERO's own controller the hand moves about 0.22 of each commanded step per tick, and the policy learned this partial motion. Trained toward the command instead of the nominal execution, the same layer succeeds in 25.6% of episodes under changes outside its training distribution, against 76.9% for the policy without a layer. In a run that records the tracking error, it raises the error to 15.4 mm, against 6.8 mm without a layer and 6.0 mm for System 0.5.

### Does System 0.5 retrain the VLA or need the parameters of System 0?
No. The VLA stays frozen, and the layer never receives the parameters of System 0. It identifies the current System 0 from its own history of commands and measured motion, using recursive least-squares statistics and an encoder that summarizes them as a 64-dimensional vector.

### How is System 0.5 trained?
In simulation, by gradients through a learned forward model and without reinforcement learning. Training copies the simulator state at each chunk's start to record the nominal execution, and the forward model's sensitivity turns other commands into the change of motion they would cause. Training replays recorded pi0.5 chunks and never queries the VLA. At deployment one tick takes about 1 ms on one CPU thread.

### What results does System 0.5 achieve?
With pi0.5 on LIBERO, System 0.5 reaches 72.7% success on RoboStress against 56.6% best reported, and 68.1% on the J-PARC joint-fault benchmark against 61.7%. Over eight System 0 changes outside its training distribution it reaches 84.7%, above all four baselines (best 79.4%), and placed unchanged below OpenVLA-OFT and GR00T N1.7 it raises their success from 59.7 to 75.6% and from 59.4 to 80.0%. On a real UR5e it lowers the tracking error from 9.0 to 1.2 mm at every one of 30 placements and lowers the median task time from 114 to 54 s.

### Does System 0.5 work with other VLA policies?
Yes, under the eight changes outside the training distribution. The layer trained on pi0.5 chunks, placed unchanged below OpenVLA-OFT and GR00T N1.7, raises their success from 59.7 to 75.6% and from 59.4 to 80.0% (one-sided bootstrap p < 0.001). Under the nominal System 0 their success does not fall (91.1 to 93.1% and 92.2 to 92.2% over 360 episodes).

### What are the limits of System 0.5?
The layer assumes that its own measurements are not delayed; on the UR5e, whose measurements are late, the second layer is trained with the measurement lag varied. On the UR5e it lowers the tracking error at every one of 30 placements and completes 21 of 30 trials against 16 without a layer (one-sided sign test p = 0.063); the change on that arm shortens every step without changing its direction, so its measured cost is time. Under a joint range limit or a lock, where no command can produce part of the motion, System 0.5 improves on base by 3.5 to 7.6 points, against 17.5 to 18.0 points under joint friction.

### Are the paper and code available?
The paper is under review and the code will be released upon publication. This page shows the method, the results and all 90 UR5e hardware trials.

## Abstract
A vision-language-action (VLA) policy is trained under one controller and robot body, its nominal System 0, but System 0 changes in use: joint faults lower the LIBERO success of pi0.5 from above 95% to below 57%. We trace such drops to the tracking error against the nominal execution, the motion that the nominal System 0 would produce for the same action chunk from the same state. We present System 0.5, a layer below a frozen VLA that identifies the current System 0 from its own history and corrects each command toward the nominal execution. It is trained on this error through a learned forward model, without any task reward. Under eight changes of System 0 absent from training, success rises more where System 0.5 lowers the error more. The same layer trained to follow the command instead lowers success from 76.9 to 25.6%. System 0.5 outperforms four baselines under these changes and exceeds the best reported mean success on our reimplementations of two joint-fault benchmarks. Retrained for a real UR5e, it lowers the tracking error by 87% and more than halves the median task time.
